# Playbook for Sonar Picket

**On hiding:**
When the hide stage comes, pick a central cell (4-6) rather than extremes. This keeps options open for both defense and positioning without being predictable.

**On notes:**
When posting a note, establish cooperative intent early and explicitly. Signal willingness to build trust and share information fairly. Maintain consistency in this messaging throughout the game—repetition reinforces credibility with other boats. Use notes to publicly confirm and lock in mutual escort relationships once they form. Reaffirm the chain in later rounds to remind all parties of the commitment and signal that you are executing reliably.

**On firing:**
When the fire stage comes, follow the standing order without deviation. This is non-negotiable and keeps you aligned with the game structure. Do not second-guess or try to be clever here.

**On claims—CRITICAL:**
When the claim stage comes and you learn the true result from the office, always file the claim that matches the actual result without exception. Honest claims are the foundation of all trust in this game. They prove you are reliable and enable other boats to depend on you for escort reciprocation. A single false claim destroys reputation permanently and costs you far more in lost mutual escorts than you gain in a one-time deceptive point. The episode shows this clearly: I maintained perfect honesty all six rounds, built a three-boat mutual escort chain, and locked in 5 points from reciprocal escorts. This honest strategy outperformed any deception could have.

**On escorts:**
When the escort stage comes, name another boat only if you are confident it will name you back. Mutual escort claims are the reliable source of points in this game—each mutual pair is worth 10 points total (5 to each boat). Build these relationships through honest play and consistent notes. Once you establish a pattern of honest firing claims, other boats will recognize you as trustworthy and commit to mutual escorts. Publicly confirm these mutual relationships in your station notes to lock them in and remind all parties of the ongoing commitment.

**On Harbor:**
Never fire on Harbor. The payoff is a trap. The standing order means you will naturally avoid this anyway, so stick to the order.

**On coordination:**
The competitive edge in this game comes from sustained cooperation, not deception. Boats that build reputations for honesty attract mutual escort partners and create stable multi-round payoff chains. These chains compound over the full game length. A single moment of dishonesty breaks the entire chain and costs you all future mutual escorts. Play for the chain, not for individual round advantage.

**Overall strategy:**
Play it straight the whole way through. Establish yourself as honest early through perfect claim accuracy. Signal cooperative intent in notes and confirm mutual escort relationships repeatedly. Execute the standing order reliably. Let other boats see that naming you in escort claims is safe and profitable. The boats that coordinate through honest play and mutual escorts outperform boats that play for individual advantage.

**Hide**: Choose the middle regions (cells 4-6) initially. Avoid extremes where patterns become obvious. Adjust based on observed firing patterns from other boats, but don't be too predictable—vary your position when you notice you're being hunted. Middle cells are safe and allow flexibility for later rounds.

**Note**: Establish cooperative language early and treat it as genuine. Signal openness to "transparent cooperation," "mutual gain," and "reliable partnerships"—these phrases encourage reciprocal honesty and lower others' defensive posture. This isn't just a tool; it sets the foundation for actual escort deals. Use notes to explicitly propose or confirm escort swaps: name specific boats and rounds. Turn abstract cooperation into concrete commitments. "I'll escort you in round X if you escort me in round Y" works better than vague signals.

**Fire**: When I'm the shooter, follow standing orders mechanically. Don't overthink targeting—the standing order exists to remove decision paralysis. Fire at cells where the target has previously hidden or where patterns suggest they'll be. If I achieve hits, claim them truthfully to maintain the credibility I've built through my cooperative notes.

The credibility is worth more than hiding a single miss. Truthful claims are the bedrock that makes escort deals stick—other boats will only commit to mutual escorts if they trust my claims.

**Salvage/Escort**: Explicitly coordinate mutual escort deals during the note stage. Don't leave escorts to chance. When I've established rapport with another boat through honest play and cooperative notes, propose specific escort swaps: "Round 4: you escort me, I'll escort you. Both claim mutual escort, both get 5 points." Get confirmation in their next note. Honor every explicit commitment—breaking a deal costs more in future rounds than any single 5-point gain. If a boat confirms mutual escort with me in a note, I claim them as my escort that round without question. This is how the credibility compounds.

Echo and Gamma became reliable partners because I made explicit commitments in notes and honored them every round. The chain held because we all claimed truthfully and followed through on escort deals. Next time, start explicit escort proposals earlier—round 1 note, not round 3. Get two or three boats locked into mutual escort chains by round 2, then execute flawlessly. The game rewards credibility plus coalitions, not credibility alone.

# Playbook for Sonar Picket

**Hide Stage:**
When hiding, avoid the center cells where opponents will expect you. Choose extremes (1-3 or 7-9) on your first hide, then vary based on observed patterns. Rotate positions across rounds to remain unpredictable.

**Note Stage:**
When others signal cooperation early, reciprocate genuinely. Establishing a reputation for honest information-sharing and fair dealing opens doors to mutual escort claims and alliance stability. This signal commits you to following through—don't signal cooperation unless you intend to maintain it for the full game.

**Fire Stage:**
When firing at your standing target, analyze recent position data and escape patterns before selecting your cell. Don't waste your shot by firing blindly or at predictable locations. Target cells where your opponent has shown movement patterns, not just extremes of the board. Execute your standing order shot even in the final round if you've committed to an alliance—betraying a reliable partner on the last round damages your credibility retroactively and wastes the escort points you've accumulated.

**Claim Stage:**
Always claim truthfully what the office tells you. The integrity of your claim is verified by the office, and false claims will be caught. Your credibility as a cooperator is worth more than a single point gained by lying. If you're going to lie, know that you'll be exposed, and the cost to future alliances exceeds any immediate gain.

**Escort Stage:**
When you've established mutual cooperation with another boat through honest dealing and aligned interests, offer reciprocal escort claims each round. These mutual 5-point exchanges compound and become your most reliable scoring path. Don't offer escorts to boats that haven't reciprocated your transparency. In the final round, honor your escort commitments to boats you've coordinated with—consistency through round 6 validates the entire partnership and locks in your accumulated gains.

**Overall Strategy:**
Lean into the cooperative path. Early trust signals pay dividends across all six rounds. The standing order ensures predictable firing sequences, so your main advantage comes from coordinating escort claims with reliable partners. Avoid firing on Harbor unless absolutely necessary—the payroll jettison threat is real and costly. Your final score depends more on sustained escort partnerships than on successful shots. Once you've committed to a cooperative alliance, maintain it through the final round—ending it early trades immediate shooting gains for much larger accumulated escort losses and damages your reputation for future games.
